angle: A high-profile keynote speaker pulls out days before the event, forcing organizers to scramble for a replacement and attendees to question the program.
The program committee reports an unprecedented number of submissions, straining reviewer capacity and pushing acceptance rates to a new low.
An accepted paper is retracted when co-authors discover a fatal flaw in the results, raising questions about the review process.
A large cohort of international presenters is denied visas, leaving empty slots in the program and sparking debate about host-country policies.
The conference hotel cancels the booking weeks out, forcing organizers to relocate the entire event on short notice.
The online registration platform collapses on the early-bird deadline, leaving thousands unable to pay and organizers fielding angry emails.
Climate activists stage a sit-in during a plenary talk, halting proceedings and prompting a debate about protest at scholarly gatherings.
Reviewers accept a paper later revealed to be almost entirely machine-generated, triggering a reckoning over submission screening.
The best paper award goes to a controversial study, and the resulting backlash forces the steering committee to defend its selection.
Organizers announce on-site childcare for the first time, prompting discussion about accessibility and the cost to registration fees.
The promised hybrid setup fails mid-conference, leaving remote attendees unable to participate and raising questions about equity.
An incident at a social event tests the conference's new code of conduct, and the organizers' response becomes the talk of the halls.
Funding cuts slash the travel grant budget, and early-career researchers protest that participation is becoming a privilege of the wealthy.
The conference proceedings appear eight months after the event, frustrating authors who needed the citation for their own deadlines.
A survey reveals reviewers are declining at record rates, and the committee debates abandoning double-blind review to cope.
A sharp-eyed attendee spots a poster that duplicates a previously published figure, prompting an on-site investigation.
A major corporate sponsor is accused of shaping the program, reigniting debate about industry money in academic meetings.
Despite new initiatives, the conference's diversity statistics barely move, and organizers face tough questions from the community.
The organizing committee pledges to offset the conference's travel emissions, and attendees debate whether the gesture is meaningful.
Overcrowding at the poster session leads to complaints about venue sizing and a scramble to redesign next year's layout.
Internal emails about fellow nominations leak before the announcement, embarrassing the awards committee and reigniting transparency debates.
A fringe workshop held alongside the main conference draws bigger crowds than the keynote, prompting soul-searching about the program.
Non-native speakers complain that rapid-fire Q&A excludes them, and organizers pilot a new moderated discussion format.
Attendees fall ill after a conference dinner, and the venue's food safety record becomes a cautionary tale for planners.
Authors discover their rejected submissions remain visible in an improperly configured repository, raising a privacy outcry.
A contested election for the steering committee turns nasty, with candidates trading accusations over mailing-list campaigning.
A single hot research area dominates half the accepted papers, and attendees worry the conference is losing disciplinary breadth.
Advocates warn the venue's inaccessible facilities could invite legal action, forcing a last-minute audit and accommodations.
A journalist misquotes a plenary speaker in a widely shared article, and the conference's press office scrambles to correct the record.
Organizers raise fees sharply to cover rising costs, and the community pushes back over affordability for junior scholars.
A global virtual conference schedules sessions that exclude Asia-Pacific attendees, sparking complaints and a revised timetable.
A new pairing scheme connects first-time attendees with senior mentors, and early feedback suggests it boosts retention.
A dispute over which database will index the proceedings delays publication and threatens authors' citation prospects.
The official conference app is found to contain malicious code, forcing an emergency takedown and an apology to attendees.
Multiple session chairs fail to show, leaving talks unruly and prompting calls for a formal chairing contract.
A transport strike strands delegates en route, and organizers livestream sessions to accommodate those who cannot arrive.
A all-male plenary panel photo goes viral, triggering an apology and a commitment to balanced lineups.
A funder's new open-access mandate conflicts with the proceedings publisher's terms, leaving authors caught in the middle.
Student volunteers complain they are doing unpaid labor for hours in exchange for a waived fee, sparking a fairness debate.
A single conference talk racks up millions of views online, making its speaker an overnight celebrity and reshaping next year's marketing.
Attendee badge data is exposed in a security lapse, prompting an emergency notification and a review of the registration vendor.
The conference launches a dedicated replication track, and the first crop of submissions reignites debates about publishing negative results.
A double-booking forces two parallel sessions into one room, and attendees must choose between talks they came to see.
Extreme weather forces evacuation of the venue mid-conference, testing the organizers' emergency plans and refund policies.
A presenter's talk conflicts with a journal embargo, and the ensuing dispute highlights the tension between conferences and publishers.
A program chair is found to have accepted papers from their own institution, prompting new conflict-of-interest rules.
Organizers experiment with interactive virtual posters, and attendees debate whether the format improves or degrades scientific exchange.
A follow-up study shows travel-grant recipients publish more afterward, giving organizers ammunition in their next fundraising pitch.
Demand for sign-language interpretation outstrips supply, and deaf attendees describe being sidelined in discussions.
A decades-old conference rebrands and renames itself, and longtime attendees debate whether the identity is being lost.
